abstract: Systemin (SlSYS1) from Solanum lycopersicum was the first plant peptide hormone to be identified, and its receptor (SYR1), processing, and role in defense are all well characterized. However, studies of systemins outside of Solanum are extremely limited. Here, we identified four new bioactive systemins within the genus Nicotiana, three from N. tabacum, NtSYS4A/B/C, and one from N. benthamiana, NbSYS4. We showed that expressing the canonical systemin receptor SlSYR1 confers the ability to detect these novel systemins. In addition, we found that LAB accession N. benthamiana contains a premature stop codon in its SlSYR1 orthologs, providing a potential basis for its insensitivity to systemins. We showed that N. tabacum roots can respond to NbSYS4, and that expressing its SYR1 homolog NtSYR1A allows for the detection of systemins in N. benthamiana. Additionally, we found that NtSYS4A can downregulate NtSYR1A-dependent ROS, akin to antisystemin (SlAntiSYS) in tomato. Our findings challenge the consensus that systemins are limited to the Solanoideae clade and uncover a new immune signaling system within Nicotiana.
